Being independent your first year of college can be done through many things like moving out on your own and not answering to anyone but yourself. But they’re other factors as well. Controlling your finances, making appointments, and being in charge of your future are just a few. Below I have put together a few points that need to be accomplished your first year of college to begin being independent.

GET A JOB

Getting a job is so important your first year of college. I personally took a summer job and transferred to a different location in the fall and thus had a job before school even started. Even if you have loans to pay for tuition and rent, extra money can be used to save or spend at your own leisure. It’s also a good way to plan ahead. When it comes to taking out loans for the next semester you can support yourself on the money you make from you job instead of taking out your max loans (like I did my first year.) Getting a job is a good way to spend free time, making money by working short shifts, a couple times a week, at a part time job can fill in the blanks when you have some free time. If it is a work-study job provided by your college or a part time job near where you live, getting a job is so important to living independently.

AVOID PROCRASTINATION

One of the main things that set a good student apart from a mediocre student is going to be how they spend their time. No matter if it’s schoolwork, applying for a scholarship, or joining a club on campus, procrastinating will either bring you to the top or sink you to the bottom. This is important to being independent because, if you aren’t getting your work done, aren’t setting your goals while actively trying to achieve them, and you’re always cutting it down to the wire, more of your time will be spent worrying about doing those things and less time doing things you want. My best advice is to schedule your time wisely so you don’t procrastinate and get stuck in a bind.

BUDGET YOUR MONEY

I didn’t really realize how important budgeting money was until my second semester of college, but it connects hand in hand with having a job. Setting a budget where you know where every penny you have is being spent, helps you be independent by not worrying about having enough money. I first realized the importance of a budget when in my first semester of college I had to ask my parents to help with rent. By budgeting my money the second semester, I didn’t have to worry at all about rent money because I had enough saved. Though being independent financially isn’t the only part of being independent, it is necessary to your success. There are many different methods of budgeting I’ve used a few like the envelope method, and the zero dollar budget but trying them out and seeing what works the best personally is the way to go. These are just three steps I have taken my first year of college that helped my become more independent. Though my points aren’t necessary, they did help me get on my feet my second semester, and I plan on following these through my next years in college. My advice to you is get a job, avoid procrastination, and budget your money!
